families.family: Query engine, deps, transitions, token budget, stop hooks
families.reason: The donor's loop handles the four things OCADE's did not: output-token recovery, reactive compaction, an explicit token budget, and a closed terminal set. Both rooms now run it, with local inference injected through callModel.

families.family: Permissions, shell rule matching, dangerous patterns, denial tracking
families.reason: Cowork's approvalPolicy and Chat had separate ideas about risk. The donor's rule model is stronger and now decides for both, with OCADE's opaque-command gate added on top.

families.family: Bash parser, heredocs, quoting, destructive-command warnings
families.reason: A real parser is what closes the compound-command hole: an approval for one command must not carry the rest of the line. Ported in pure TypeScript, without the donor's native grammar binary.

families.family: Task lifecycle, stop, background tasks, status labels
families.reason: OCADE had a to-do board and no runtime task state at all. The donor's status machine, id scheme, pause accounting and stop error taxonomy now back Stop, Pause, Resume and Take over.
OCADE remembered only what the model chose to record. The donor's thresholds decide when a conversation is worth summarising without re-summarising it every turn.

families.family: Memory record shapes and the age/relevance model
families.reason: Freshness decay and memory typing were absent on the OCADE side.

families.outcome: Ported — donor replaced a weaker OCADE version
families.reason: OCADE's stripper missed the Unicode Tag block, so instructions could be smuggled into text that looked clean. The donor's sanitiser covers it; the old regex is gone.

families.family: Message protocol: content blocks, tool use, tool results
families.reason: One shape for the transcript, converted once at the engine boundary.

families.family: Tool search and deferred tool loading
families.outcome: Not ported — OCADE keeps its own
families.reason: The donor's tool search depends on the hosted API's tool_reference beta blocks, which no on-device runtime accepts. OCADE defers by domain and caps each turn at a measured twelve tools, which is the same problem solved for a local model.

families.outcome: Not ported — OCADE's is stronger here
families.reason: OCADE already decomposes a goal once and runs each step as a sub-agent with only that step's tools, returning one line to the main transcript. The donor's version assumes concurrent hosted sessions, which one local model cannot serve.

families.outcome: Not ported — OCADE keeps one authority
families.reason: The donor loads plugins from the user's filesystem at startup and trusts what it finds. OCADE's registry validates and trusts packs explicitly, which is the model a browser product can actually honour.
The donor bridge speaks to a hosted relay. OCADE's browser work goes through the extension and machine work through the paired companion; neither needs a server in the middle.
A tab has no pseudo-terminal, and shipping one would mean shipping a second renderer. Shell work belongs to the companion, behind the permission layer.

families.family: Hosted inference, provider table, OAuth to the model vendor
families.reason: OCADE answers on the device. There is no hosted-AI fallback anywhere in the path, and the audit that proves it runs in CI.
The donor logged events on nearly every decision. Nothing about how someone uses OCADE leaves their device.

families.outcome: Not ported — OCADE keeps its own
families.reason: The donor's session history is a paginated read against a hosted events API. OCADE's sessions are local first and mirrored to the account, which is the opposite direction.

families.outcome: Not ported — OCADE keeps its own
families.reason: OCADE's scheduler already reports why each automation did not run — paused, not due, backing off, awaiting approval — which is the part users ask about.

families.outcome: Not ported — OCADE keeps its own
families.reason: The donor's voice layer is terminal command plumbing. OCADE's speaks through the device's own speech services and stays on the same runtime as the rest of the session.

families.outcome: Not ported — kept behind the local boundary
families.reason: Repository work needs a filesystem, so it lives with the companion rather than in the tab. OCADE exposes it through the same tool runtime instead of shipping a second coding product.
Launch is free. The code is intact and hardened — signature checks, idempotency, replay refusal — and every purchase action is behind a gate nobody can get through.
